previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and diffuse body pain, including right hip pain, after a prolonged decline in well-being. She has a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, type 1 diabetes with complications, gastroparesis, fibromyalgia, and chronic pain. Admission evaluation revealed hyponatremia, fluid overload, and drug-induced constipation likely exacerbated by opioid use. There was no evidence of infection on blood or dialysis fluid cultures, and imaging showed no acute abnormalities. An irrigation of the peritoneal cavity was performed to improve dialysis efficacy. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, medication adjustments, and reduced opioid use. She was discharged home with optimized pain management, continued peritoneal dialysis, and follow-up plans with her specialists.

of SOB, orthopnea, cough, nausea, weight gain.  Found to be 
hyponatremic and uremic, and with elevated peritoneal fluid cell 
count consistent with peritonitis.  She was started on 
intraperitoneal ABx, her peritoneal cell counts downtrended with 
IP ABx, and her uremia and hyponatremia improved with PD.

ACTIVE ISSUES
====================
# Peritonitis:  Initial cell count on peritoneal fluid showed 
910 WBC and 57% PMN's, consistent with peritonitis.  This likely 
worsened her nausea and abdominal pain, and made dialyzing her 
more difficult.  IP Vancomycin and Ceftazidime were started on 
___.  Transplant Surgery was consulted, but did not recommend 
catheter removal or surgery.  Cultures showed no growth.  
Peritoneal cell counts downtrended promptly with IP Antibiotics. 
 She will continue IP Vanc/Ceftaz as an outpatient and finish 
the course of ___, ordered by her new PD center.

# Orthostatic Hypotension:  Patient had positive orthostatics, 
generally at nighttime after PD.  Possibly in setting of 
challenging her dry weight from dialyzing.  However, another 
major contributor was her nausea and poor PO intake during the 
day, as she is unable to take good PO intake due to 
distension/fullness of abdomen during daytime PD dwells.  This 
should improve with moving to home, where she can get PD at 
night.  However, her home Lasix was stopped as well.

# ESRD
# Uremia
# Hyponatremia
# Weight gain, dyspnea, orthopnea:
Her presenting symptoms of dyspnea and orthopnea likely 
developed in the setting of volume overload from suboptimal PD.  
This is supported by her hyponatremia, as well as uremia (70's 
on last discharge, 110's on admission here).  Overall she was 
satting well on room air, CXR with no obvious pulm edema, and 
she was overall hemodynamically stable.  PD was continued in 
house.  Her BUN improved with dialysis.  She was set up with a 
new PD center prior to discharge.

# Diarrhea:  Frequent loose stools ___.  C-Diff negative.  
Improved with conservative treatment

# Anemia:  Hgb low but stable this admission, with no e/o 
bleeding.  Likely predominantly due to ESRD.  Iron studies and 
haptoglobin within normal limits.  Reticulocyte index was low, 
indicating likely a hypoproliferative anemia.  Remained stable 
throughout hospital course.
 
# Acute on Chronic Nausea, abdominal pain:  
# Gastroparesis:  
Her GI symptoms are likely related in part due to history of 
gastroparesis, but worsened by inadequate dialysis with uremia 
and abdominal distension on admission, as well as peritonitis.  
Her peritonitis was treated, and she was dialyzed.  She was 
treated with Zofran and IV Ativan as needed for nausea.  Her 
symptoms were also worsened by the inability to do peritoneal 
dialysis cycles overnight on her hospital floor, thus limiting 
her PO intake due to abdominal distension during the day.
   
# DM1:  Consulted ___ while inpatient, and continued on home 
Insulin regimen of Lantus including carb counting.

# Constipation: Attributed to opioid induced constipation in the 
past, no longer on opioids.  Continued home bowel regimen.

# Seasonal Allergies: Continue home loratadine  

# Chronic pain: Continued home pregabalin, tizanidine, and 
nortriptyline
